sentences.text: Unless the order passed by the Magistrate is perverse or the view taken by the court is wholly unreasonable or there is nonconsideration of any relevant material or there is palpable misreading of records, the revisional court is not justified in setting aside the order, merely because another view is possible.
The revisional court is not meant to act as an appellate court.
The whole purpose of the revisional jurisdiction is to preserve the power in the court to do justice in accordance with the principles of criminal jurisprudence.
Revisional power of the court under Sections 397 to 401 of Cr.PC is not to be equated with that of an appeal.

Unless the finding of the court, whose decision is sought to be revised, is shown to be perverse or untenable in law or is grossly erroneous or glaringly unreasonable or where the decision is based on no material or where the material facts are wholly ignored or where the judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or capriciously, the courts may not interfere with Ashish decision in exercise of their revisional Rastogi jurisdiction."

Regarding the said statements it is observed that not a single specific detail has been mentioned with respect to the date, time and month as to when the said incidents took place.
It is trite law that the allegations have to be specific and the charges cannot be framed on general and omnibus allegations.
Principles of justice and equity also demand that the Accused should also be given a fair opportunity to put forth his defence so as to prove his innocence.

One of the reasons why Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble Delhi High Court have repeatedly cautioned the Trial Court not to proceed on the basis of general and omnibus allegations is that if such kind of allegations are proceeded upon, then the accused shall be deprived of his chance to prove his innocence against the said allegations.

An example to elucidate this point is that if specific allegations are mentioned, then one of the defences which can be taken by the Accused is that of Alibi and to prove the same it shall be permissible for him to adduce his evidence but said defence is not at all available to the Accused in case of general and omnibus allegations.

Whoever dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use property, knowing that such property was in the possession of a deceased person at the time of that person's decease, and has not since been in the possession of any person legally entitled to such possession, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the offender at the time of such person's decease was employed by him as a clerk or servant, the imprisonment may extend to seven years.

sentences.text: In the present case, the petitioners being the own brothers of the deceased and the deceased living jointly with them, it cannot be said that the property left by the deceased Ashish was not in the possession of these petitioners also, or that these petitioners were not legally Rastogi entitled to such possession.

I find myself in agreement with the law laid down by the Calcutta High Court in Harendra Nath Mandal's case (supra), that a person may not have title to the property in the sense of the title to the ownership of the property, but yet he may be legally entitled to the possession thereof.

If the person is either entitled to the possession of the property of the deceased, or at the time of the deceased he was also possessing the property along with the deceased, being his close relative, no offence can be said to be made out against such person under Section 404 of the Indian penal Code.
25. In this case also, the alleged withdrawal has been made by the Class-I heirs of the deceased who are his own mother and real brother respectively.

The fact whether they were legally entitled to the said amount is a question which may be determined by a civil court and enough civil remedies are available to the Revisionist for recovery of the said amount.
To prosecute the Respondents under Section 404 IPC would essentially means that this Court assumes that they were not legally entitled to the said amount.

Even if the case laws as cited by the Ld. Sr. Counsel are considered, the withdrawal from the bank account may be considered to be a violation under Banking regulations Act for which specific consequences flowing from the said act may follow but not the penal consequences under IPC.

26. Even if for the sake of the argument it is assumed that they were not legally entitled for withdrawing the said amount, then also it cannot be assumed that there was an overwhelming criminal intent present right from the Ashish Rastogi inception for dishonest misappropriation of the property CR No.83/2025 Reshma Gupta v. Neeraj & Anr. by Ashish Rastogi Date: 2026.03.06 18:09:41 +0530 possessed by the deceased at the time of his death.

Also, as rightly observed by the Ld. Trial Court, the Complaint, in which the said allegations have cropped up for the first time, was lodged 4 months after the death of the deceased while the money was withdrawn immediately after his death.
There is no justification as to the fact that if the mobile phone of the deceased was misused and the money was transferred without her consent then why no complaint was preferred against the same.
Hence, this Court finds no infirmity in the order of the Ld. Trial Court in discharging the Accused persons/Respondents from the offence under Section 404/34 IPC also.

27. In the light of above discussion, it is the considered opinion of this Court that no perversity or illegality can be found in the order of the Ld. Trial Court so as to warrant any interference by this Court in the exercise of its Revisionary jurisdiction and hence the Revision Petition Digitally stands dismissed.
